done_when: The owner switches a repo to agent merges with one command run in their own terminal

findings.body: The replacement matches only a bare `merge` key at column one. [TOML permits indentation and quoted keys](https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0), so a valid `forge.toml` containing `  merge = "human"` or `"merge" = "human"` passes the initial config check. `_switched` then inserts a second top-level merge key, commits invalid TOML, and `forge close` fails. Rerunning the command leaves the duplicate key in place. Replace the existing top-level key in these valid forms.
findings.title: Handle valid indented or quoted merge keys

findings.body: `forge fix start "Enable" --done ...` can create `fix/enable` because the existing slug logic accepts that name (`src/forge/task.py:204-210`). For that ready fix, `forge merge enable` now always enters `_enable` instead of merging the item. It refuses from an agent shell or, when agent merges are already on, as already enabled. The valid fix can no longer be merged through Forge.
findings.title: Preserve merging an existing fix named enable

findings.body: New evidence beyond the close/merge guard ruling: a differently named fix that changes `merge` reaches Ready in an unsigned prototype. `forge close` correctly says a human merges (`src/forge/close.py:142`), but this condition sees the prototype's effective agent setting (`src/forge/repo.py:174-177`) and prints `Next: forge merge <item>`. That command then refuses the merge (`src/forge/merge.py:59-60`). `forge next` should give the owner-merge step for any fix whose head changes the merge setting.
findings.title: Keep forge next on the owner path for other merge-setting fixes

why: Nothing in the flow can switch a repo to agent merges: Forge tells the owner to ask the agent, and the agent's own permission checks rightly refuse to loosen a gate on itself
